# R_heldout — first measurement on sequences that were never selected on

## Verdict

The held-out 95% CI excludes the dev-split claim on TSR. Pooled held-out TSR is 0.210 [0.115, 0.325] versus the dev 0.512, and FAR is 0.236 [0.142, 0.339] versus the dev 0.280. The dev-split headline is not reproduced on sequences the knobs were not selected on.

## Protocol

Shipped configuration only, no ablation: `scripts/run_target.py` ships with `--ablate` defaulting to
`"all"`, which would run the entire 84-variant grid — an ablation sweep, forbidden here.
`build_variants("")` is also mapped to `"all"`, so the CLI cannot express "baseline only".
This script therefore pins `run_target.build_variants` to a baseline-only builder inside its own child
process and asserts each summary contains exactly one variant, `baseline`.

- command per sequence: `python scripts/run_target.py --data-root data/raw/dancetrack/val/<seq> --mask none --max-frames 300 --subsample 2 --jobs 2 --out results/heldout_dancetrack/<seq>`
- single-sequence selection: `discover_sequences` returns `[root]` when `--data-root` already is a sequence dir
- sweep guard: every included summary has `meta.variants == ["baseline"]` (asserted, not assumed)
- pooling: frame-weighted over `n_report_frames`; error bars from a **cluster bootstrap over sequences**
  (2000 reps, seed 0, resampling whole sequences with replacement — frames within a sequence are not independent)

### Spread / diagnosis

The per-sequence spread is not a rounding artefact — it is the finding:

- 7 of 22 sequences sit below TSR 0.05: `dancetrack0025`, `dancetrack0035`, `dancetrack0058`, `dancetrack0063`, `dancetrack0065`, `dancetrack0081`, `dancetrack0090`
- 2 of 22 sit above TSR 0.80: `dancetrack0079`, `dancetrack0094`
- 5 of 22 have FAR > 0.50 (wrong-identity lock dominant): `dancetrack0010`, `dancetrack0014`, `dancetrack0018`, `dancetrack0073`, `dancetrack0090`
- Pearson r between the auto-picked target's median visible height and its TSR is **-0.016** (target heights 153-736 px): success is *not* explained by how big the clicked target was, so 'the held-out targets are just tiny' is not a valid explanation of the drop.
- mean 272 ms/frame; per-sequence report frames 92-300 (hence frame-weighted pooling).

## Comparison against the dev-split claim

| | TSR | FAR |
|---|---|---|
| dev split (n=3, same 3 sequences used to choose every knob) — `docs/EXPERIMENTS.md:1390-1395` | 0.512 | 0.280 |
| **held-out (n=22)** | **0.2102** | **0.2364** |
| delta | -30.18 pp | -4.36 pp |
| held-out 95% CI covers the dev claim? | **no** | yes |

Dev per-sequence spread for context (`docs/EXPERIMENTS.md:1390-1395`): 0004 0.415/0.040, 0005 0.695/0.205,
0007 0.426/0.595 — i.e. the dev 'mean' is already the average of a 0.040-FAR and a 0.595-FAR sequence.

**How weak the dev claim was, recomputed from its own three rows** (`docs/EXPERIMENTS.md:1392-1394`): TSR mean 0.512, sd 0.159, 95% t-interval ±0.394 → [0.118, 0.906]. FAR mean 0.280, sd 0.285, 95% t-interval ±0.708 → [-0.428, 0.988]. The audit's ±0.394 is this interval, reproduced exactly. A ±0.394 bar on a 0.512 estimate is wider than the whole gap to the 0.55 target, which is why the dev number certified nothing.
